method: Verse-by-verse preliminary screening of Quran 2:251–260, comparison with accessible Qur'anic Arabic and 1 Samuel 17 critical translation notes; original Hebrew/Greek collation incomplete. No candidates verified for publication. Reconcile with main and private queue before merge.

verses.finding: David kills Jalut/Goliath and receives kingship and wisdom; 1 Samuel 17:48–51 shares the victory, but does not place David's accession at that instant.
Revelatory authentication of the preceding account; no source-specific earlier parallel assigned.
Prophets differ in rank, Jesus is supported by holy spirit, followers dispute; earlier Christian texts warrant separate research, no single precise counterpart established.
Exhortation to give before final judgment; no specific earlier passage established in this pass.
Throne verse: divine sovereignty, knowledge and preservation; no single earlier text assigned; comparative throne imagery needs a dedicated dossier.
No compulsion in religion, right guidance and false gods; do not equate with earlier tolerance formulas without contextual verification.
God as patron of believers versus false patrons; no precise textual association established.
Abraham debates a ruler about giving life and death and the sun; no secure pre-Islamic narrative locator verified in this pass.
Person passes ruined settlement, dies and revives after a hundred years; no precise pre-Islamic counterpart assigned; Ezekiel 37 is only a possible broad resurrection motif.
Abraham requests a demonstration of resurrection with four birds; no precise earlier bird-resurrection story established; Genesis 15:9–11 is a potential contrast, not an identical narrative.

candidates.shared: David defeats and kills Goliath/Jalut during Israelite conflict.
candidates.difference: Samuel specifies sling, stone and sword and separates later accession; Qur'an summarizes the victory and God's granting of rule and wisdom.

candidates.shared: Abraham and multiple birds appear in a divinely directed scene.
candidates.difference: Genesis concerns a covenant ceremony with divided animals and birds, not resurrection or birds called back to life; not a direct parallel.

questions: Collate 1 Samuel 17 Hebrew, shorter Greek form and 4QSam(a) where extant; do not conflate manuscript dates with composition.
Check possible pre-Islamic Abraham and four-birds traditions beyond Genesis 15 before linking 2:260.
Examine Ezekiel 37 carefully before proposing a 2:259 comparison.
Resolve open overlapping research PRs and verify private queue and RLS before publication.
